devices.name: ber1-tor-b
devices.apply_note: No WAN path lands here, so a bad change costs one half of the rack's redundancy rather than the site's connectivity. Always the first switch changed, and the only one used to try a change out.
devices.note: Carries a spare LR optic, pre-provisioned so WAN failover is a matter of moving the LC jumper rather than sourcing hardware. Its port is not recorded yet.

devices.name: ber1-tor-a
devices.apply_note: Carries the WAN optic and the router uplink, so a bad change takes the site off the internet and takes the path used to fix it with it. Changed only after the same change has been applied to ber1-tor-b and the rack is still up.

devices.name: ber1-mgmt
devices.apply_note: There is one management switch and it is the path to JetKVM, AMT and ATS monitoring. Losing it loses out-of-band access to everything else at once, so it is changed alone, last, and only once both ToRs are known good. Its uplinks go straight to ber1-edge and never through a ToR, so a ToR change cannot isolate it.

edge.description: WAN termination and the path every other node reaches the internet through

services.description: DHCP, DNS, NTP and the tailnet subnet router

runner.description: Mac mini running the runner fleet

nodes.name: ber1-edge
nodes.note: Dual-homed, one SFP+ DAC to each ToR, on an Intel X710 that takes TL-SM5220 DACs.

nodes.name: ber1-store-a
nodes.note: Single-homed to ToR A. The storage pair is split one node per ToR, the same way it is split across opposite ATS chains, so losing a ToR costs one storage node and not both. Moving these onto one switch would quietly remove that.

nodes.name: ber1-svc
nodes.note: Single-homed to ToR B today, which puts DHCP, DNS, NTP, the tailnet subnet router and half the runners behind one switch. A seventh DAC would dual-home it; add the second link here when it arrives.

nodes.name: ber1-store-b
nodes.note: Not bought yet, arriving November, and the only one of the four x86 nodes still to come. Single-homed to ToR B as the other half of the storage pair. In the prep bay it is the empty slot in racknex #2 beside ber1-svc.

placement.runner: A Mac mini has one NIC, so it lands on exactly one ToR. Minis are split A/B across the two ToRs the same way the power feeds are, so losing a ToR costs half the fleet rather than all of it.
placement.storage: One storage node per ToR, matching the split across opposite ATS chains. Losing a ToR must cost one storage node, never both, so ber1-store-a is on ToR A and ber1-store-b on ToR B. The fleet tests enforce it.
